groups.title: Authoring schema, deterministic generation and explicit bindings
groups.explanation: The schema/version, thirteen-theme order, formatting and raw-only semantic bindings are local reproducibility constraints. The compiler supports typed components; the generator intentionally supports a subset.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Retain generation checks; do not generalize this subset into the complete compiler schema.

groups.title: Identity, structure, typed payloads and component admission
groups.explanation: Canonical identities and fixed structure are project constraints. Eight hex digits validate payload shape, not RGB interpretation. CT_INVALID/automatic/index/system values need distinct semantics.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Preserve identities and payload types; document CT_COLORINDEX as retained compatibility debt. Do not infer literal RGB from the payload shape.

groups.title: Cosmora reversible raw-color mappings
groups.explanation: Bidirectional color mapping is a project identity invariant, not a Microsoft token contract.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Retain split/merge guards across all three shifted variants.

groups.title: Numeric contrast helpers and threshold decisions
groups.explanation: The older helper rounds blended channels and adds 0.0001 tolerance. The newer helper preserves fractional channels and compares directly. An actual helper probe changes a 4.4916975 failure into a 4.5144298 pass.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Use one consumer-aware calculation path later; separate display/source quantization from threshold decisions.

groups.title: Generic same-color text pairing and exceptions
groups.explanation: Unclassified raw pairs are still treated as normal text. Three diff exclusions correct known cases, but XML Foreground/Background names are not a general content contract.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Restrict enforced content pairings to identified consumers; retain unknown pairings as screening evidence.

groups.title: Hard-coded shell content and status context pairs
groups.explanation: Four SystemFill status tokens are explicitly classified as normal text at 4.5 despite the documented stroke/border role. Other text pairings still require their declared underlays.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Split status strokes from message text and select actual neighboring surfaces before changing thresholds.

groups.title: Context registry schema and source-contract enforcement
groups.explanation: The module validates typed references, complete alpha chains and thresholds, but a confirmed-contract label does not require a rendering mode or traceable consumer evidence. Each of 69 entries is separately assessed.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Record consumer/rendering provenance in step 2; retain unresolved states until corroborated.

groups.title: Registered editor RGB surfaces
groups.explanation: The 52 registered components correctly require opaque RGB and use explicit fill/border/hatch kinds. Their thresholds are project requirements. This does not cover every editor color.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Retain these checks and extend only for a traced consumer. Check overlap and actual rendered states later.

groups.title: Active legacy states and inherited overlay foregrounds
groups.explanation: Selected accent and inherited-foreground relationships encode previous design decisions; eight registered overlay paths now require opaque RGB.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Keep raw/inherited types separate; confirm remaining legacy active consumers during runtime work.

groups.title: Legacy text, links, surfaces and state pairs
groups.explanation: Explicit role names improve classification, but many links and borders are checked against a shared secondary/tertiary surface rather than a traced parent.
groups.recommendedDisposition: For each member, inspect its control template and active/inactive parent chain; preserve source anchors pending evidence.

groups.title: Disabled and decorative treatment
groups.explanation: Disabled exemptions, a 1.5 discoverability advisory, and the stricter disabled scrollbar glyph rule are local policy. A non-focused enabled window is not a disabled control.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Keep disabled/active semantics distinct and label stronger project rules accordingly.

groups.title: Neutral modern control and card ladders
groups.explanation: The control ladder matches documented alpha tiers, with intentional palette-derived RGB. The three card tiers differ from current Dark reference values, contradicting the authoring guide's shared installed-Dark claim.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Correct provenance wording or conduct a later deliberate card review; do not silently copy Dark colors.

groups.title: Legacy neutral fills and pressed-state distinctions
groups.explanation: 0x18 neutral hover, dark pressed lifts, engaged-command accents and exact state distinctions are local design requirements.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Retain project intent; trace actual parent surfaces before promoting state-pair estimates to consumer evidence.

groups.title: Strong borders, focus indicators and separator advisories
groups.explanation: The semantic focus/stroke distinction is appropriate, but uniform secondary-surface tests do not establish all adjacency or focus states. PanelSeparator is correctly advisory.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Trace each declared focus/border consumer and its adjacent surfaces; retain separator estimates as advisory.

groups.title: Razor, HTML, CSS and variable hierarchy
groups.explanation: Semantic aliasing, opaque variable anchors, inherited members and OKLab separation are project design rules.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Retain family distinctions; keep named types and renderer semantics separate from color similarity.

groups.title: Active editor selection content coverage
groups.explanation: Core syntax surface checks omit active selection; only selected foreground and variables receive dedicated checks. Installed normal selection painting uses the background brush. Fifty-nine of 273 registered syntax/active-fill source pairs fail 4.5.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Extend the active-syntax matrix after confirming normal-selection presentation; keep high-contrast selection behavior separate.

groups.title: Find and symbol marker semantics and prominence
groups.explanation: The inspected marker contract distinguishes outline and fill. Border colors, borderless choices and OKLab strength floors are project requirements.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Retain consumer-scoped marker interpretation; verify intersecting markers and state precedence at runtime.

groups.title: Current-line and inactive selection safeguards
groups.explanation: Inactive fills have explicit opaque coverage. Current-line source pins exist for ten themes; remaining current-line checks allow composition and do not establish all types or overlap behavior.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Inspect CurrentLineActiveFormat in each unpinned theme and confirm brush/pen use and selection overlap before extending opaque assertions.

groups.title: Amberroot statement and code-analysis overlays
groups.explanation: Six checks enforce an alpha-composited normal-text model without a traced consumer. CodeAnalysisKeyEventSelection is simultaneously unresolved as F06-063 in the contextual registry.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Resolve each statement/analysis consumer, its RGB conversion and foreground meaning; remove contradictory confidence claims before remediation.

groups.title: Core syntax anchors, markup coupling and distances
groups.explanation: Exact family anchors and perceptual separation are local design policies; the Plain/Operator pair is exempt from the entire distance check, not only exact equality.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Document the actual exemption and retain explicit family/member lists. Active-selection gap is DR-016.

groups.title: Hardline neutral edges and debugging exception
groups.explanation: Quiet versus meaningful edges and the debugging-purple exception are approved design choices, not High Contrast system mode.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Preserve the explicit exception and avoid making a Windows High Contrast claim.

groups.title: Shell base, headers, tool panes and Foundation neutral surfaces
groups.explanation: Matching modern/legacy surfaces and Foundation charcoal are project cohesion rules. The reference does not require these equalities across custom themes.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Retain the approved neutral anchors; track modern and legacy consumer paths separately.

groups.title: Legacy solution-name state treatment
groups.explanation: The low-alpha active legacy title and separate inactive text are project relationships; modern badge validation is separate.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Preserve the separation; do not use a legacy title check to qualify the modern badge.

groups.title: Layered document-tab/toolbar equality
groups.explanation: A 0x4D layer, exact secondary/tab composition, lighter-than-base direction and 0.02 distance encode the custom design; the official default values do not establish a universal elevation ordering.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Retain as project policy with an explicit underlay and later visual verification.

groups.title: Modern solution badge and shared toolbar frame
groups.explanation: Installed templates confirm the token consumers and shared border. Exact title/toolbar fill equality is the user-approved project choice; official defaults differ.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Keep shared semantic binding and identify the exact candidate during future runtime review.

groups.title: Resting and operational status bars
groups.explanation: A 30% black resting band and darker-than-body direction are local styling constraints; operational text contexts are separate.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Preserve state distinctions and qualify the underlay in runtime evidence.

groups.title: Scrollbar state ladder
groups.explanation: 3/3.5/4.5 state ratios, increasing contrast, 0.03 distances and disabled arrow discoverability are stronger local policies rather than a WCAG state ladder.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Retain these thresholds as project decisions and verify DPI, glyph and adjacency effects later.

groups.title: Extension Manager surface gap constraints
groups.explanation: Shelf/list/page equalities and tight distances preserve historical source assumptions. Current nested consumer surfaces and runtime reachability are not established here.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Trace Cider/CommonDocument templates and compare the actual Extension Manager state against the retained measurements.

groups.title: Per-theme palette pins and variant anchors
groups.explanation: Named palette anchors and stable variants express the custom theme identities, including the approved Foundation review.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Preserve raw mappings and theme identities; open any later recolor as a separate reviewed change.

groups.title: Editor hyperlink content and Output URL rendering
groups.explanation: F04-043 assumes an alpha blend. Output urlformat defaults to bBackgroundValid=0, which removes the background brush; if a theme override supplies a valid background, the inspected conversion produces opaque RGB. Final override validity is unresolved. Thirteen RGB-branch ratios fail, while all thirteen ignored-background ratios pass.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Inspect final Output URL format properties and validity flags for the current package; register either inherited underlay or opaque RGB as evidenced. Do not bake a foreground-only item based on the conditional numbers.

groups.title: Coverage reports, advisories and acceptance limits
groups.explanation: Coverage output explicitly describes its bounded scope and retains unresolved results; inventory dispositions are not a complete map of specialized checks. Test success is not runtime acceptance.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Keep counters and evidence scopes separate, preserve historical artifact identities, and reconcile inventories in step 2.

groups.title: Authoring/release workflow and documentation-only rules
groups.explanation: Locked palettes, semantic editing, explicit generation, proportionate tests, runtime evidence and no token deletion by RGB coincidence are project maintenance requirements.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Retain these safeguards. Documentation claims with specific mismatches are separately linked to findings.

groups.title: Known inline-diagnostic message and border contract
groups.explanation: The version-matched Roslyn implementation sets message foreground, border background brush and transparent interior; F06-059 through F06-061 use the editor underlay.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Retain this contract and separate diagnostic URL links; overlap still needs runtime inspection.

groups.title: Current notification window versus legacy notification pairings
groups.explanation: The inspected UserNotificationsWindow item template uses ToolWindowText and ToolWindowBackground, with notification hover/selection brushes. It does not reference the registered legacy title/subtitle tokens.
groups.recommendedDisposition: Locate any alternate consumers of the legacy pairs; register the inspected template separately. Absence here is not proof the old tokens can be deleted.

Amberroot is intentionally mid-tone rather than uniformly dark. Its shell base,
secondary, and elevated surfaces use warm olive-charcoal layers, while
`Text Editor Text Manager Items/Plain Text` retains the darker `#1C1E19`
editor anchor. Amber owns primary actions, sage owns attention and secondary
emphasis, lighter sage owns enabled links and strings, and mineral blue keeps
semantic locals and parameters distinct. Do not collapse the editor into the
mid-tone shell or reinterpret the amber/sage relationship as a conventional
warning/success pair. Amberroot numbers use a brighter mineral-orange family
than its amber keywords, while types and markup use a lighter sage than
strings. Its current-statement overlays are deliberately weaker than ordinary
accent overlays so their preserved foregrounds remain readable.

quaternary `#202024`, above the existing `#0E0E11` shell and `#151518` secondary

`#172325`/`#172627` surface family, including headers, tabs, tool panes, and
related decorative grays. `SupportingTertiary`, `SupportingQuaternary`, and
the `DecorativeGrey*` anchors retain the other themes' existing values.
Foundation's blue interaction accents and semantic syntax colors keep their
separate roles. See [the Foundation surface review](audits/FOUNDATION_NEUTRAL_SURFACES.md).

Bubblegum direction. Its supplied pink, raspberry, lavender, cyan, rose-text,

rules.guidance:
Nullsector is a dark, semi-dystopian cyberpunk theme whose color behaves like
signal traffic rather than decoration. Near-black editor and shell surfaces
stay quiet; acid lime owns primary action, selected command, and genuine
keyboard-focus meaning; cyan owns links, properties, and informational
emphasis. The editor selection remains a restrained blue-black surface.
Strings use signal green, numbers hazard amber, types cyan, methods violet,
markup hot pink, comments telemetry slate, and locals/parameters electric blue.
The active selection and subdued cyan inactive RGB fill are deliberately
subdued so all registered syntax retains `4.5:1`. Do not spread acid lime into
ordinary rest, hover, or pressed controls: its scarcity is what gives
Nullsector its operational identity.

Silverphase is a role-aware gallium-inspired theme. Its supplied background,
surface, elevated-surface, accent, keyword, string, and border anchors remain
exact. Derived steel and cyan values support text hierarchy, links, methods,
types, focus, and selection without replacing the conventional success,
caution, and critical families. Strings retain luminous cyan, semantic locals
and parameters use a separate electric blue, and keywords retain the supplied
violet anchor.

rules.guidance:
Hardline is a role-aware high-contrast-inspired industrial theme. Asphalt-black
surfaces and reflective neutral text establish its readability, technical steel
owns links and semantic variables, and dark galvanized blue owns selection.
Safety orange is reserved for primary interaction, focus, active controls, and
keywords; caution yellow, signal red, and clearance green retain warning,
critical, and success meaning. Do not replace selection with orange or introduce
decorative hazard striping into IDE surfaces. Hardline is not represented as a
Windows High Contrast accessibility theme. Methods use caution yellow `#FFE066`, comments use a warmer concrete neutral, and ordinary dividers use
quiet steel `#42484B`. Control outlines, focus borders, scrollbar borders, and
other meaningful edges retain strong steel `#697277`; the purple debugging
status is an intentional functional exception.

rules.guidance: Razor and HTML roles follow semantic anchors rather than independent colors: element names use the markup/type color, attribute names use the property color, values use the string color, delimiters/operators use the muted comment color, entities use the number color, and Razor components/directives use the keyword color. rules.guidance:
Semantic locals and parameters form one variable family per theme. The Roslyn
`local name` and `parameter name` roles must match the C++
`CppGlobalVariableSemanticTokenFormat`, `CppLocalVariableSemanticTokenFormat`,
and `CppParameterSemanticTokenFormat` roles. Variable foregrounds are opaque,
pass normal and selected-editor contrast, remain at least `0.08` OKLab from
inherited plain/member text, and remain at least `0.06` from keywords, methods,
and types. Fields, properties, and events retain `CT_INVALID` foreground
semantics so they inherit the theme's neutral editor text. This is a semantic
hierarchy invariant, not permission to recolor unrelated syntax families.

Legacy `Environment` roles do not consistently use XML component names according to
rendering semantics. `ThemeRolePolicy.psd1` therefore classifies single-component
content, glyphs, surfaces, links, disabled roles, state pairs, semantic borders,
inactive-selection syntax, contextual editor overlays, syntax distances, and
Hardline's neutral-versus-meaningful edge policy.
Update that policy and its regression fixtures whenever an intentional palette review
changes one of those relationships. Do not infer that a component named `Background`
is necessarily a fill.

Primary foreground reuse is not itself a state-collapse defect: official Dark uses
the same primary text across several focused, hovered, and pressed controls. Generic
control surfaces and strokes, however, must use the palette-neutral interaction
registry rather than opacity tiers of `AccentFillDefault`.

rules.explanation: The control ladder matches documented alpha tiers, with intentional palette-derived RGB. The three card tiers differ from current Dark reference values, contradicting the authoring guide's shared installed-Dark claim.
rules.recommendedDisposition: Correct provenance wording or conduct a later deliberate card review; do not silently copy Dark colors.
rules.guidance:
Modern neutral control and card fills use the installed Dark alpha hierarchy over
each theme's `TextFillPrimary` RGB. Legacy hover surfaces use the registered `0x18`
neutral lift, pressed surfaces use `33000000`, and hover strokes use `0x66` over
`TextFillSecondary`. Combo-box and drop-down pressed borders use
`ControlStrongStrokeDefault`. `CommandBarMouseDownBorder` and
`CommandBarSelectedBorder` remain accent because they represent engaged or selected
commands. Genuine keyboard focus retains the theme-specific
`FocusStrokeInner`/`FocusStrokeOuter` pair. These relationships are build-blocking
semantic invariants; do not restore accent-colored generic fills or outlines when
authoring another theme.

Legacy document tabs are dark surfaces even when their XML components are named
`Background` for text and glyph content. Selected tab surfaces use
`SolidBackgroundFillSenary`, last-active and inactive provisional tabs use
`SolidBackgroundFillSecondary`, and their enabled content uses primary or secondary
text according to state. Do not restore light tab surfaces with dark text: that
reintroduces the legacy document-tab polarity defect still covered by the shared
role policy.

rules.explanation: A 0x4D layer, exact secondary/tab composition, lighter-than-base direction and 0.02 distance encode the custom design; the official default values do not establish a universal elevation ordering.
rules.recommendedDisposition: Retain as project policy with an explicit underlay and later visual verification.
rules.guidance:
Visual Studio 2026's modern document tab channel is a separate layered surface.
`ShellInternal/EnvironmentLayeredBackground` must use the theme's registered
`0x4D` palette-derived overlay. After composition over
`Shell/SolidBackgroundFillBase`, it must equal both
`Shell/SolidBackgroundFillSecondary` and `ShellInternal/EnvironmentTab`, be
perceptually lighter than the shell, and remain at least `0.02` OKLab away from
it. Do not make this role opaque or copy the legacy
`Environment/FileTabChannelBackground`; those tokens serve different rendering
paths.

rules.guidance:
The Visual Studio 2026 main shell uses one continuous base surface. The modern
`ShellInternal/EnvironmentBackground` and `EnvironmentBody` roles and all seven
legacy `EnvironmentBackground*`/texture aliases must match
`Shell/SolidBackgroundFillBase`. The resting status bar is intentionally
`4D000000`: Visual Studio composites that 30% black overlay over the shell body,
preserving each palette hue while creating the darker bottom band. Validate
resting status text against the composited result. Do not apply this relationship
to tool-window bodies, tool-window headers, editor backgrounds, or the building,
debugging, and solution-loading status states.

rules.explanation: 3/3.5/4.5 state ratios, increasing contrast, 0.03 distances and disabled arrow discoverability are stronger local policies rather than a WCAG state ladder.
rules.recommendedDisposition: Retain these thresholds as project decisions and verify DPI, glyph and adjacency effects later.
rules.guidance:
Scrollbar state is a functional hierarchy, not decorative palette reuse.
`Environment/ScrollBarBackground` remains the track anchor, while the registered
opaque resting, hover, and pressed thumb colors must reach `3:1`, `3.5:1`, and
`4.5:1` against that track and remain perceptibly ordered. Thumb and arrow
glyphs must reach `3:1`. Derive new-theme ladders in OKLab toward the theme's
secondary text, round once to deterministic eight-bit sRGB, and register the
result in `ThemeRolePolicy.psd1`; do not collapse the thumb back into the track.

rules.explanation: The inspected marker contract distinguishes outline and fill. Border colors, borderless choices and OKLab strength floors are project requirements.
rules.recommendedDisposition: Retain consumer-scoped marker interpretation; verify intersecting markers and state precedence at runtime.
rules.guidance:
Editor markers must be classified by `MarkerFormatDefinition` semantics.
For these roles, the XML `Background` component supplies the marker fill and
the `Foreground` component supplies its outline; the foreground does not
replace syntax text. Definition and reference markers therefore require
palette-specific `CT_RAW` outlines, while matched-selection and scope markers
are intentionally borderless. Expression-hover and Find markers use caution
outlines. Do not restore `CT_INVALID/00000000` on every marker foreground: that
removes the functional outlines and collapses definition/reference hierarchy.

rules.explanation: Inactive fills have explicit opaque coverage. Current-line source pins exist for ten themes; remaining current-line checks allow composition and do not establish all types or overlap behavior.
rules.recommendedDisposition: Inspect CurrentLineActiveFormat in each unpinned theme and confirm brush/pen use and selection overlap before extending opaque assertions.
rules.guidance:
Find, definition, reference, matched-selection, scope, current-line, and
selection surfaces use opaque RGB values in the registered editor formats.
Every registered enabled
syntax family must retain `4.5:1`; meaningful marker outlines must retain
`3:1` against both the editor and effective fill. Outlined marker fills use a
restrained baked-color treatment: authored Find and reference fills remain
at least `0.06` and `0.04` OKLab from the editor, and Find remains at least
`0.01` stronger than reference. Current-line surfaces remain at
least `0.06` from the editor but no stronger than inactive selection.
Inactive-selection anchors are change-controlled because the entire 273-pair
matrix passes; changing one requires an explicit regression and renewed runtime
review.

rules.guidance:
`EditorSurfacePolicy.json` additionally registers diff, merge, hatching, brace,
Peek, snippet, coverage, and call-return consumers. Its fill/editor contrast
ceiling of 2.5 and repeated-hatching range of 1.1 to 2.0 are project comfort
limits, not WCAG requirements. Syntax still requires 4.5:1 and meaningful word
borders require 3:1. Diff word foregrounds are borders; overview foreground
also draws the empty-region hatching and viewport pen. Do not assign text or
notification accents to these surfaces. Shell alpha policies remain separate.
See [the editor RGB remediation evidence](audits/EDITOR_RGB_SURFACE_REMEDIATION.md).

rules.explanation: Exact family anchors and perceptual separation are local design policies; the Plain/Operator pair is exempt from the entire distance check, not only exact equality.
rules.recommendedDisposition: Document the actual exemption and retain explicit family/member lists. Active-selection gap is DR-016.
rules.guidance:
Core editor syntax is governed by semantic paths, never by source-value search
and replacement. `CoreSyntaxFamilyRoles` synchronizes Roslyn and C++ methods,
types, variables, comments, numbers, and operators against per-theme opaque
anchors. Every registered family must retain `4.5:1` through the editor,
inactive selection, current line, Find, definition, reference, scope, matched
selection, and expression hover. Unrelated families require `0.06` OKLab
separation; values below `0.08` are advisory. Plain text and core punctuation
may intentionally share a neutral lane, but no other exact collision is
allowlisted.

rules.guidance:
Keep C# `field name`, `property name`, and `event name` foregrounds inherited
with `CT_INVALID`. Do not include line numbers, inlay hints, whitespace,
adornments, or marker fills in a semantic recolor merely because they share an
RGB value. Type-coupled markup elements and muted markup delimiters must retain
their documented relationships. A new or changed syntax family needs an exact
policy anchor, a mutation fixture, composited-surface validation, and runtime
review in the dense C#/C++/Razor/HTML/CSS fixture.

rules.explanation: Installed templates confirm the token consumers and shared border. Exact title/toolbar fill equality is the user-approved project choice; official defaults differ.
rules.recommendedDisposition: Keep shared semantic binding and identify the exact candidate during future runtime review.
rules.guidance:
Visual Studio 2026's solution-name box uses `ShellInternal/EnvironmentBadge`.
It shares the `ToolbarLayeredBackground` authoring anchor with
`ShellInternal/EnvironmentLayeredBackground`, matching the movable toolbar's
fill and alpha over the shell base. Both installed control templates already
use `ShellInternal/EnvironmentLayeredBorder` for their frame. Keep this badge
free of accent tints and validate primary text against its composited fill.
The legacy `MainWindowSolutionNameActiveBackground` retains its separate
`0x0F` primary-text overlay; its inactive background retains the shell base.
Those legacy roles do not control the modern badge. See
[the solution-title consumer evidence](audits/SOLUTION_TITLE_TOOLBAR_ALIGNMENT.md).
